notes.母湯: Spells the sound of Taiwanese 毋通 m̄-thang, "must not" — the characters are only the sound.
notes.歸剛: Spells Taiwanese 規工 kui-kang, "the whole day"; the meme adds 欸 (歸剛欸).
notes.阿雜: A Taiwanese word (a-tsa̍p) written with sound-alike characters.
notes.盤子: Taiwanese phân-á, "plate": someone easily served up — a sucker.
notes.蛤: Just the sound of the Taiwanese "hannh?"; the character means clam.
notes.魯蛇: Sound-spelling of English "loser" — 魯 and 蛇 carry no meaning here.
notes.吃土: Literally "eating dirt": nothing left to spend on food.
notes.爆雷: Taiwan says 爆雷／有雷／防雷; 劇透 is the China term you will also see online.
notes.飯糰: Sticky rice wrapped around 油條 youtiao, pickled radish and pork floss.
notes.有雷: The warning tag on PTT / Dcard threads; 防雷 marks a spoiler-free zone.
notes.是在哈囉: Sarcastic; Dcard / PTT slang from around 2019.
notes.泡麵番: As long as it takes to cook instant noodles: a three-minute episode.
notes.機車: Literally a scooter. Calling someone 機車 has nothing to do with riding one.
notes.拍謝: A Taiwanese apology written with Mandarin characters for the sound; nobody reads it as pāixiè.
notes.秀逗: From the English "short" by way of Japanese ショート — a short circuit.
notes.踹共: 出來講 said fast in Taiwanese, then written back in Mandarin characters.
notes.犁田: Literally ploughing a field — what your body does to the tarmac.
notes.北七: 白痴 said in Taiwanese, then written back with the characters that carry the sound.
notes.沙發: From the English "sofa": the first person to sit down in the thread.
notes.頭香: From the first stick of incense of the new year at a temple: the same race to be first.
notes.網路: Taiwan says 網路 where the mainland says 網絡.
notes.甜不辣: From the Japanese てんぷら, written with characters that carry the sound.
notes.乳酪: Taiwan says rǔ luò where the mainland says rǔ lào.
notes.佛跳牆: The name says even a monk would climb the wall for it.
notes.垃圾桶: Taiwan says lèsè where the mainland says lājī.
notes.牽手: In Taiwanese 牽手 is the word for a wife — the one whose hand you took.
notes.垃圾: lèsè in Taiwan, lājī on the mainland — the same two characters.
notes.黑白切: Literally "cut at random": you point and the boss slices.
notes.般若: Read bō rě, not bān ruò: a Sanskrit sound kept in old characters.
notes.數位: Taiwan says 數位 where the mainland says 數字.

variantNotes.藉口: 藉口 is the Taiwan standard spelling; 借口 is what most people type online.
variantNotes.阿們: Protestant churches write 阿們; Catholic ones write 阿門.
variantNotes.飯糰: Shops write 飯糰 or 飯團; both are common.
variantNotes.豆干: Menus write 豆干 or 豆乾; both are common.

food: 老闆，滷肉飯大碗一碗，加一顆滷蛋。

夜市的蚵仔煎要淋很多甜辣醬才好吃。

蚵仔煎的蚵仔要新鮮，粉漿要薄。|Kēzǎijiān de kēzǎi yào xīnxiān, fěnjiāng yào báo.|The oysters in an oyster omelette must be fresh and the batter thin.||逛夜市一定要吃一份蚵仔煎。|Guàng yèshì yīdìng yào chī yī fèn kēzǎijiān.|A night-market visit is not complete without an oyster omelette.

珍珠奶茶是台灣最有名的飲料。|Zhēnzhū nǎichá shì Táiwān zuì yǒumíng de yǐnliào.|Bubble milk tea is Taiwan's most famous drink.||下午三點，辦公室一起訂珍珠奶茶。|Xiàwǔ sān diǎn, bàngōngshì yīqǐ dìng zhēnzhū nǎichá.|At three in the afternoon the office orders bubble tea together.
這家牛肉麵的湯頭很濃郁，麵條也很有嚼勁。

牛肉麵的牛肉要燉到軟才行。|Niúròumiàn de niúròu yào dùn dào ruǎn cái xíng.|The beef in beef noodle soup has to be stewed until tender.||台北每年都有牛肉麵節，大家都去排隊。|Táiběi měinián dōu yǒu niúròumiàn jié, dàjiā dōu qù páiduì.|Taipei holds a beef-noodle festival every year, and everyone goes to queue.
早餐店的蛋餅加起司是我的最愛。
Zǎocāndiàn de dànbǐng jiā qǐsī shì wǒ de zuì'ài.
Breakfast-shop egg crepe with cheese is my favorite.

蛋餅要加玉米還是鮪魚？|Dànbǐng yào jiā yùmǐ háishì wěiyú?|Corn or tuna in your egg crepe?||早餐店阿姨煎的蛋餅外皮酥酥的。|Zǎocāndiàn āyí jiān de dànbǐng wàipí sūsū de.|The egg crepe the breakfast-shop lady makes has a crisp outside.
我每天早上都喝一杯溫豆漿。
Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang dōu hē yī bēi wēn dòujiāng.
I drink a cup of warm soy milk every morning.
豆漿要冰的還是熱的？|Dòujiāng yào bīng de háishì rè de?|Soy milk cold or hot?||這家的豆漿是自己磨的，沒有加糖。|Zhè jiā de dòujiāng shì zìjǐ mó de, méiyǒu jiā táng.|This shop grinds its own soy milk and adds no sugar.
傳統飯糰裡面包了油條、菜脯和肉鬆。
Chuántǒng fàntuán lǐmiàn bāo le yóutiáo, càipú hé ròusōng.
A traditional rice roll is stuffed with fried dough, pickled radish and pork floss.

早餐店的飯糰要加辣還是不辣？|Zǎocāndiàn de fàntuán yào jiā là háishì bù là?|Spicy or not for your breakfast-shop rice roll?||紫米飯糰比白米的更有嚼勁。|Zǐmǐ fàntuán bǐ báimǐ de gèng yǒu jiáojìn.|A purple-rice roll is chewier than a white-rice one.
中午我們去買排骨便當好不好？
Zhōngwǔ wǒmen qù mǎi páigǔ biàndāng hǎo bù hǎo?
Shall we get pork-chop bento for lunch?

火車上的便當有排骨和滷蛋。|Huǒchē shàng de biàndāng yǒu páigǔ hé lǔdàn.|The bento on the train has a pork chop and a braised egg.||媽媽每天早上幫我準備便當帶去學校。|Māma měitiān zǎoshang bāng wǒ zhǔnbèi biàndāng dài qù xuéxiào.|Mom packs a bento for me to take to school every morning.
這家的炸排骨又大又香。
Zhè jiā de zhá páigǔ yòu dà yòu xiāng.
The fried pork chop here is huge and fragrant.

排骨要先醃再炸，才會入味。|Páigǔ yào xiān yān zài zhá, cái huì rùwèi.|Pork chops need marinating before frying to take on the flavour.||這碗湯裡的排骨燉得很軟。|Zhè wǎn tāng lǐ de páigǔ dùn de hěn ruǎn.|The pork ribs in this soup are stewed till tender.
滷肉飯配一碗貢丸湯，就是台灣人的日常。
Lǔròufàn pèi yī wǎn gòngwántāng, jiù shì Táiwān rén de rìcháng.
Braised pork rice with a bowl of meatball soup is everyday life in Taiwan.

這碗貢丸湯的湯頭很清甜。|Zhè wǎn gòngwántāng de tāngtóu hěn qīngtián.|The broth of this meatball soup is light and sweet.||夜市攤位的貢丸湯一碗三十塊。|Yèshì tānwèi de gòngwántāng yī wǎn sānshí kuài.|A bowl of meatball soup at the night-market stall is thirty dollars.
燙青菜我要地瓜葉，加一點蒜頭醬油。
Tàng qīngcài wǒ yào dìguāyè, jiā yīdiǎn suàntóu jiàngyóu.
For blanched greens I'll have sweet potato leaves with a bit of garlic soy sauce.

地瓜葉炒蒜頭，簡單又下飯。|Dìguāyè chǎo suàntóu, jiǎndān yòu xiàfàn.|Sweet potato leaves stir-fried with garlic: simple, and it goes great with rice.||阿嬤在菜園裡種了一大片地瓜葉。|Āmà zài càiyuán lǐ zhòng le yī dà piàn dìguāyè.|Grandma planted a big patch of sweet potato leaves in the vegetable garden.
晚上肚子餓，我們去買鹹酥雞配九層塔。
Wǎnshang dùzi è, wǒmen qù mǎi xiánsūjī pèi jiǔcéngtǎ.
Hungry at night, we went for popcorn chicken with basil.

鹹酥雞要加九層塔和辣粉才對味。|Xiánsūjī yào jiā jiǔcéngtǎ hé làfěn cái duìwèi.|Popcorn chicken only tastes right with basil and chili powder.||巷口那攤鹹酥雞每天都大排長龍。|Xiàngkǒu nà tān xiánsūjī měitiān dōu dàpáichánglóng.|The popcorn chicken stall at the end of the lane has a long queue every day.
外國朋友第一次聞到臭豆腐都嚇一跳。
Wàiguó péngyǒu dì yī cì wén dào chòudòufǔ dōu xià yī tiào.
Foreign friends always get a shock the first time they smell stinky tofu.

臭豆腐要配泡菜一起吃才對。|Chòudòufǔ yào pèi pàocài yīqǐ chī cái duì.|Stinky tofu should be eaten with pickled cabbage.||深坑的臭豆腐是碳烤的，跟夜市炸的不一樣。|Shēnkēng de chòudòufǔ shì tànkǎo de, gēn yèshì zhá de bù yīyàng.|Shenkeng's stinky tofu is charcoal-grilled, unlike the fried kind at the night market.
冬天最適合跟朋友一起吃火鍋了。
Dōngtiān zuì shìhé gēn péngyǒu yīqǐ chī huǒguō le.
Winter is the perfect time for hot pot with friends.

火鍋的湯底我喜歡麻辣的，他喜歡昆布的。|Huǒguō de tāngdǐ wǒ xǐhuān málà de, tā xǐhuān kūnbù de.|For hot-pot broth I like spicy; he likes kelp.||吃到飽的火鍋店，一個人五百塊。|Chīdàobǎo de huǒguō diàn, yī ge rén wǔbǎi kuài.|The all-you-can-eat hot-pot place is five hundred a person.
Lǎobǎn, zài lái yī pán tàng qīngcài.
Boss, one more plate of blanched greens.

燙青菜上面淋的是蒜頭醬油和肉燥。|Tàng qīngcài shàngmiàn lín de shì suàntóu jiàngyóu hé ròuzào.|What is drizzled on the blanched greens is garlic soy sauce and minced-pork sauce.||吃太油了，我們點一盤燙青菜平衡一下。|Chī tài yóu le, wǒmen diǎn yī pán tàng qīngcài pínghéng yīxià.|We have had too much greasy food; let us order a plate of blanched greens to balance it.
宵夜買一袋滷味回家配電視。
Xiāoyè mǎi yī dài lǔwèi huí jiā pèi diànshì.
For a late-night snack, grab a bag of braised goodies to eat in front of the TV.

滷味攤的海帶和豆干是我的必點。|Lǔwèi tān de hǎidài hé dòugān shì wǒ de bìdiǎn.|Kelp and dried tofu from the braised-snack stall are my must-orders.||看球賽的時候，一定要配滷味和啤酒。|Kàn qiúsài de shíhòu, yīdìng yào pèi lǔwèi hé píjiǔ.|Watching a ball game, you have to have braised snacks and beer.
Taiwanese meatball in translucent glutinous dough
彰化的肉圓是炸的，台南的是蒸的。
Zhānghuà de ròuyuán shì zhá de, Táinán de shì zhēng de.
Changhua's meatballs are fried; Tainan's are steamed.

肉圓的皮很有彈性，醬料是甜的。|Ròuyuán de pí hěn yǒu tánxìng, jiàngliào shì tián de.|A Taiwanese meatball's skin is nicely springy, and the sauce is sweet.||下午三點，肉圓店門口已經在排隊了。|Xiàwǔ sān diǎn, ròuyuán diàn ménkǒu yǐjīng zài páiduì le.|At three in the afternoon there is already a queue outside the meatball shop.
我要一碗乾麵，不要加辣。
Wǒ yào yī wǎn gānmiàn, bù yào jiā là.
One bowl of dry noodles, no chili.

這家的乾麵拌的是自製的肉燥。|Zhè jiā de gānmiàn bàn de shì zìzhì de ròuzào.|This shop tosses its dry noodles with homemade minced-pork sauce.||老闆，乾麵一碗，湯麵一碗，外帶。|Lǎobǎn, gānmiàn yī wǎn, tāngmiàn yī wǎn, wàidài.|Boss, one dry noodles, one soup noodles, to go.
乾麵配餛飩湯是小吃店的經典組合。
Gānmiàn pèi húntuntāng shì xiǎochīdiàn de jīngdiǎn zǔhé.
Dry noodles with wonton soup is the classic snack-shop combo.

天冷的時候來一碗餛飩湯最舒服。|Tiān lěng de shíhòu lái yī wǎn húntuntāng zuì shūfú.|When it is cold, a bowl of wonton soup is the most comforting thing.||餛飩湯裡加一點芹菜和油蔥更香。|Húntuntāng lǐ jiā yīdiǎn qíncài hé yóucōng gèng xiāng.|Wonton soup smells even better with a little celery and fried shallot.
早餐店的蘿蔔糕煎得酥酥的，加蛋更好吃。
Zǎocāndiàn de luóbogāo jiān de sūsū de, jiā dàn gèng hǎochī.
The breakfast shop fries its turnip cake nice and crisp; it's even better with an egg.

過年的時候，媽媽會自己蒸蘿蔔糕。|Guònián de shíhòu, māma huì zìjǐ zhēng luóbogāo.|At Chinese New Year, Mom steams her own turnip cake.||我的早餐是一份蘿蔔糕加一杯豆漿。|Wǒ de zǎocān shì yī fèn luóbogāo jiā yī bēi dòujiāng.|My breakfast is a turnip cake and a cup of soy milk.
吃火鍋一定要沾沙茶醬。
Chī huǒguō yīdìng yào zhān shāchájiàng.
You have to dip in shacha sauce when eating hot pot.

沙茶醬拌麵也很好吃，不只是火鍋沾醬。|Shāchájiàng bàn miàn yě hěn hǎochī, bù zhǐshì huǒguō zhànjiàng.|Shacha sauce is great tossed with noodles too, not only as a hot-pot dip.||牛肉炒空心菜要加一匙沙茶醬才夠味。|Niúròu chǎo kōngxīncài yào jiā yī chí shāchájiàng cái gòuwèi.|Beef stir-fried with water spinach needs a spoon of shacha sauce to have enough flavour.
小菜來一盤滷豆干和海帶。
Xiǎocài lái yī pán lǔ dòugān hé hǎidài.
For sides, a plate of braised dried tofu and kelp.

豆干炒芹菜是一道很家常的菜。|Dòugān chǎo qíncài shì yī dào hěn jiācháng de cài.|Dried tofu stir-fried with celery is a very homely dish.||大溪的豆干很有名，很多人去買。|Dàxī de dòugān hěn yǒumíng, hěn duō rén qù mǎi.|Daxi is famous for its dried tofu; lots of people go there to buy it.

星期天全家一起包水餃。|Xīngqītiān quánjiā yīqǐ bāo shuǐjiǎo.|On Sunday the whole family wraps dumplings together.||水餃沾醬油和一點辣油最對味。|Shuǐjiǎo zhàn jiàngyóu hé yīdiǎn làyóu zuì duìwèi.|Dumplings dipped in soy sauce and a little chili oil taste just right.
I'd like a portion of pan-fried dumplings.

鍋貼底部煎得金黃酥脆才好吃。|Guōtiē dǐbù jiān de jīnhuáng sūcuì cái hǎochī.|Pot stickers are only good when the bottoms are fried golden and crisp.||我們點了十個鍋貼和一碗酸辣湯。|Wǒmen diǎn le shí ge guōtiē hé yī wǎn suānlàtāng.|We ordered ten pot stickers and a bowl of hot and sour soup.
這家的餛飩很大顆，湯也好喝。
Zhè jiā de húndùn hěn dà kē, tāng yě hǎohē.
The wontons here are big, and the soup is good too.

媽媽包的餛飩皮薄餡多。|Māma bāo de húndùn pí báo xiàn duō.|The wontons Mom wraps have thin skins and lots of filling.||冷凍餛飩煮三分鐘就可以吃了。|Lěngdòng húndùn zhǔ sān fēnzhōng jiù kěyǐ chī le.|Frozen wontons are ready after three minutes of boiling.

隔夜飯拿來做炒飯最剛好。|Géyè fàn ná lái zuò chǎofàn zuì gānghǎo.|Day-old rice is perfect for fried rice.||這盤蝦仁炒飯粒粒分明，很香。|Zhè pán xiārén chǎofàn lìlì fēnmíng, hěn xiāng.|This shrimp fried rice has every grain separate, and it is fragrant.

白飯免費續碗，配菜另外算。|Báifàn miǎnfèi xù wǎn, pèicài lìngwài suàn.|Free refills on plain rice; side dishes are charged separately.||這鍋滷肉太鹹了，要多配一點白飯。|Zhè guō lǔròu tài xián le, yào duō pèi yīdiǎn báifàn.|This pot of braised pork is too salty; it needs more plain rice.
